transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use it again: the burning-rubber smell means the brush-drive area has overheated and it needs checking by a qualified engineer before it is switched on again. The suction motor is still doing its job, so the likely fault is local to the floorhead: most commonly a hair/thread jam or a slipping/snapped drive belt; less often the brush-bar motor or drive mechanism has failed. With it unplugged only, turn the head over and look for tightly wound hair or thread around the roller and both ends; see whether the roller will turn freely by hand. That observation will help distinguish a jam from a belt or motor fault, but it must not be used again even if the roller is cleared.

ok its unplugged n i turned it over. brush turns by hand but its tight, theres loads of hair n a bit of tassel wrapped round the ends. the burnin smell was only right when it stopped, no sparks or electrical smell tho

That tangle is very likely the original cause. A tight, hair-bound roller can make the rubber drive belt slip and produce a brief burning-rubber smell, while the hose suction stays normal. Keep it unplugged, use scissors carefully (avoid cutting bristles), and remove all hair and tassel from the roller and especially the ends; gloves can help. Once clear, the roller should spin easily rather than feeling tight. If it still binds, or if it becomes free but the brush still will not run, the next likely issue is a heat-damaged, stretched or snapped drive belt and the floorhead will need its belt/drive checked before use.
ok cut all the hair n tassel off, it spins free by hand now. what should i do next?

That should have fixed the original problem: the hair and tassel had tightened around the brush roller, making it bind and likely causing the belt to slip briefly, hence the burning-rubber smell. As it now spins freely by hand and there were no sparks or electrical smell, it is reasonable to use it again normally. Check and clear the roller ends regularly—especially after carpets, pet hair or tassels—to prevent it happening again. If the brush still does not rotate during use, stop and unplug it; the drive belt is then the most likely part to have been stretched or damaged by the jam.

Brush-bar motor or floorhead drive fault (medium)
